mode of production.context_notes: Formal term; “उत्पादन प्रणाली” may be used for broader prose, but not as a casual substitute.

surplus labor.context_notes: Essential political economy term; do not use casual words.

commodity.context_notes: Prefer in Marxian analysis; “वस्तु” is too broad.
commodity.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

feedback.context_notes: In cybernetic and systems engineering contexts, transliterate as फीडबैक.

algorithm.context_notes: Use modern transliterated Devanagari for computing terms.

proletariat.context_notes: Formal class category; not all poor people.

means of production.context_notes: Includes tools, machinery, land and materials; not machinery alone.
means of production.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

productive forces.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

relations of production.context_notes: Use for property and class relations in production.
relations of production.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

superstructure.context_notes: Formal Marxist term; do not use “ऊपरी ढाँचा.”

use value.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

exchange value.context_notes: Do not equate automatically with market price.
exchange value.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

value.context_notes: In labour theory, do not use “कीमत.”
value.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

price.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

labour.context_notes: Prefer in technical political-economy prose over “काम.”
labour.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

labour power.context_notes: A distinct Marxian category: the worker's capacity to labour, sold as a commodity under capitalism.

labour process.context_notes: Formal term in the analysis of production.
labour process.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

abstract labour.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

concrete labour.context_notes: Use as the counterpart of “अमूर्त श्रम.”
concrete labour.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

socially necessary labour time.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

surplus value.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

surplus labour.context_notes: Labour beyond necessary labour, not simply overtime.
surplus labour.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

necessary labour.context_notes: Labour needed to reproduce the value of labour-power.
necessary labour.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

constant capital.context_notes: Marx’s value category; do not confuse with fixed capital.

fixed capital.context_notes: Keep distinct from “स्थिर पूँजी”; add English on first use if necessary.

reproduction.context_notes: Renewal of production and its social conditions.

turnover of capital.context_notes: The cycle and renewal time of capital.

rate of surplus value.context_notes: Do not merge with rate of profit.

tendency of the rate of profit to fall.term: tendency of the rate of profit to fall
tendency of the rate of profit to fall.preferred: मुनाफे की दर में गिरावट की प्रवृत्ति
tendency of the rate of profit to fall.context_notes: Translate as a tendency, not as an unconditional or mechanically universal prediction.

rent.context_notes: Preferred in Marxian agrarian political economy; “किराया” is usually too narrow.

differential rent.context_notes: Formal category; do not use “अलग लगान.”

absolute rent.context_notes: Formal category in Marx’s theory of ground rent.

landed property.context_notes: Social/legal form of property in land.

finance capital.context_notes: Do not use as a synonym for money capital.

imperialism.context_notes: Use the formal Leninist political-economy term.

bourgeoisie.context_notes: Do not use “मध्यवर्ग” as its general substitute.

lumpenproletariat.context_notes: Established term; do not make it a blanket label for poor people.

dictatorship of the proletariat.context_notes: Established Hindi Marxist form. “सर्वहारा की तानाशाही” may be retained where that is the source edition’s wording.

social democrat.context_notes: Use especially for Lenin-era parties and activists.

socialism.context_notes: Established political-economic term; do not reduce it to welfare policy.

communism.context_notes: Use the established term for the Marxist social formation and movement.

anarchism.context_notes: Doctrine, not a synonym for disorder.

marxism.context_notes: General name of the theory and tradition.

materialist approach.context_notes: Use where the source is not naming the formal doctrine.

social structure.context_notes: Use for a society’s structure; not necessarily “अधिरचना.”

social contradiction.context_notes: Use where class relations are the source of the contradiction.

historical epoch.context_notes: Preferred for a distinct historical period.

social formation.context_notes: Choose “सामाजिक संरचना” when the source emphasizes composition or arrangement.

structure.context_notes: Choose “सामाजिक संरचना” when the source emphasizes composition or arrangement.

private ownership.context_notes: Use for ownership as a social relation.

collective ownership.context_notes: Do not confuse with state ownership without context.

political economy.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

production.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

production system.context_notes: Use for an organized system of production.
production system.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

labour-power.context_notes: Distinct from labour; the worker’s capacity to work.
labour-power.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

wages.context_notes: Payment for labour-power in everyday translation; retain context in technical passages.
wages.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

exploitation.context_notes: Formal class relation, not merely harsh treatment.
exploitation.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

division of labour.context_notes: Use for the social or technical division of labour.
division of labour.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

social division of labour.context_notes: Use where production is distributed across society.
social division of labour.category: Political economy: production, labour and value

capital.context_notes: Do not replace with “धन” in formal analysis.

capitalism.context_notes: The social system, not simply trade or commerce.

centralization.context_notes: Use for the concentration of control or capital through merger/absorption.

concentration.context_notes: Use for growth of capital/production in fewer or larger units.

circulation of capital.context_notes: The movement of capital through its forms.

consumption.context_notes: Do not use “खपत” in formal political-economy prose.

average profit.context_notes: Use in the transformation and equalization discussion.

interest.context_notes: Payment for the use of loaned money/capital.

credit.context_notes: Use in banking and commercial-credit contexts.

loan.context_notes: Choose contextually; “साख” may be used for creditworthiness.

money.context_notes: Formal economic term; specify “मुद्रा-पूँजी” where relevant.

currency.context_notes: Formal economic term; specify “मुद्रा-पूँजी” where relevant.

money capital.context_notes: Do not use as a synonym for finance capital.

landowner.context_notes: Use for the owner of landed property.

peasant.context_notes: Determine from context whether class position requires a more precise term.

farmer.context_notes: Determine from context whether class position requires a more precise term.

cultivator.context_notes: Useful in general economics or legal discussion.

agrarian crisis.context_notes: Use where the crisis concerns agricultural social relations or production.

class interest.context_notes: Use for interests grounded in class position.

exploited class.context_notes: Use where exploitation is the defining relation.

oppressed class.context_notes: Use where oppression, rather than exploitation alone, is central.

working class.context_notes: Use when the source is broader or less technical than “सर्वहारा वर्ग.”

wage worker.context_notes: Useful when wage relation is being emphasized.

capitalist class.context_notes: Use where ownership of capital is specifically emphasized.

artisan.context_notes: Use for small independent producers where appropriate.

trade union.context_notes: Retain the established loan expression; “मजदूर संघ” may be added on first use.

workers’ movement.context_notes: Use for organized collective activity, not isolated protest.

labour movement.context_notes: Use for organized collective activity, not isolated protest.

state power.context_notes: Use for control over the state’s coercive/political power.

capitalist state.context_notes: Use for the state in capitalist society.

colonialism.context_notes: Do not use merely for foreign influence.

reform.context_notes: A specific change; not a political tendency.

tactics.context_notes: Use for concrete methods and immediate manoeuvres.

economy.context_notes: General term for the economic system.

economic growth.context_notes: Use for quantitative expansion, often output or income.

gross domestic product.context_notes: Use “सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (GDP)” on first occurrence.

competition.context_notes: Use in market and monopoly analysis.

reserve army of labour.context_notes: Use only for the Marxist concept, not for unemployment in general.

economic crisis.context_notes: Use for systemic crisis; specify financial or balance-of-payments crisis where necessary.

inequality.context_notes: Add “आर्थिक” or “आय” where precision is needed.

productivity.context_notes: Output relative to labour, time or other inputs.
